senses.definition: to solemnly renounce a belief, cause or claim
senses.example: He abjured his former political views in a public letter.

senses.definition: not self-indulgent, especially when eating and drinking
senses.example: An abstemious man, he never had more than one glass of wine.

senses.definition: a person who renounces a religious or political belief or principle
senses.example: The party treated him as an apostate after he changed sides.

senses.definition: to raise a difficult subject for discussion
senses.example: She found it hard to broach the subject of money with her parents.

senses.definition: to tolerate or allow something, typically something unwelcome
senses.example: The coach brooks no excuses for lateness.

senses.definition: a small stream
senses.example: A brook ran along the bottom of the garden.

words.note: As a verb, brook means to tolerate and is almost always used in the negative.

senses.definition: including a wide variety of things; all-embracing
senses.example: Her catholic tastes in music ranged from opera to punk.

words.note: In lowercase, catholic means broad or universal.

senses.definition: the use of many words where fewer would do, especially in a deliberate attempt to be vague or evasive
senses.example: The spokesman's circumlocution fooled no one.

senses.definition: to combine two or more texts, ideas or sets of information into one, often wrongly
senses.example: Many people conflate weather with climate.

senses.definition: denoting or relating to the kind of language used by ordinary people; colloquial
senses.example: The novel's demotic dialogue captures the voices of the street.

senses.definition: something regarded as worthless; rubbish
senses.example: The editor sifted the gems from the dross.

senses.definition: insolent or impertinent behavior
senses.example: She had the effrontery to ask for a reference after quitting without notice.

senses.definition: having the quality of softening or soothing the skin
senses.example: The cream has emollient properties.

senses.definition: attempting to avoid confrontation or anger; calming or conciliatory
senses.example: She answered the angry letter in emollient terms.

senses.definition: to instruct or urge someone to do something
senses.example: The doctor enjoined him to rest for a week.

senses.definition: to prohibit someone from performing a particular action by issuing an injunction
senses.example: The court enjoined the company from selling the drug.

senses.definition: pressing; demanding
senses.example: The flood created exigent circumstances.

senses.definition: to atone for guilt or sin
senses.example: He tried to expiate his crimes through years of charity work.

senses.definition: to deny or contradict; to speak against or oppose
senses.example: No one could gainsay the force of her argument.

senses.definition: obtrusively bright and showy; lurid
senses.example: The bar was decorated in garish colors.

senses.definition: to gather or collect something, especially information or approval
senses.example: The documentary garnered several awards.

senses.definition: unsophisticated and socially awkward
senses.example: It would be gauche to discuss money at the dinner table.

senses.definition: overly theatrical or melodramatic in character or style
senses.example: His histrionic outburst over a parking ticket embarrassed everyone.

senses.definition: grayish white
senses.example: His hoary beard reached his chest.

senses.definition: old and trite
senses.example: The comedian told a hoary joke about mothers-in-law.

senses.definition: an extremely happy, peaceful or picturesque episode or scene, typically an idealized or unsustainable one
senses.example: Their summer on the island was an idyll.

senses.definition: (of a fortified position) unable to be captured or broken into
senses.example: The castle was thought impregnable.

senses.definition: unable to be defeated or destroyed; unassailable
senses.example: The team built an impregnable lead in the first half.

senses.definition: showing a casual lack of concern; indifferent
senses.example: She gave an insouciant shrug when told she was late.

senses.definition: showing or feeling hesitancy; uncertain
senses.example: The irresolute leader changed his mind three times in a week.

senses.definition: the state or feeling, often pleasant, of tiredness or inertia
senses.example: A pleasant languor came over us after lunch.

senses.definition: a state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy
senses.example: The fever left him with a lingering lassitude.

senses.definition: (of a liquid) free of anything that darkens; completely clear
senses.example: We swam in the limpid water of the lake.

senses.definition: (of writing or music) clear and easily comprehended
senses.example: Her limpid prose makes difficult ideas seem simple.

senses.definition: to give a lot of public attention and approval to someone; to treat as a celebrity
senses.example: The young poet was lionized by the literary world.

senses.definition: money, especially when regarded as sordid or distasteful or gained in a dishonorable way
senses.example: He gave up the stage for filthy lucre.

senses.definition: the mistaken use of a word in place of a similar-sounding one, often with an amusing effect
senses.example: Saying "dance a flamingo" for "dance a flamenco" is a malapropism.

senses.definition: to treat someone very indulgently or overprotectively
senses.example: His parents mollycoddled him until he left home.

senses.definition: a newly coined word or expression
senses.example: "Selfie" was a neologism not so long ago.

senses.definition: a medicine, especially one that is not considered effective, prepared by an unqualified person
senses.example: The peddler sold nostrums that claimed to cure everything.

senses.definition: a pet scheme or favorite remedy, especially for bringing about some social or political reform
senses.example: The candidate repeated the usual nostrums about tax cuts.

senses.definition: general or widespread hatred or disgust directed toward someone as a result of their actions
senses.example: The company earned public odium by polluting the river.

senses.definition: (of a person's voice) resonant and imposing
senses.example: The actor's orotund voice filled the theater.

senses.definition: (of writing or style) pompous; pretentious
senses.example: The report's orotund style hid its thin content.

senses.definition: extreme poverty; destitution
senses.example: The artist died in penury.

senses.definition: (of an account or representation) clearly expressed and easily understood; lucid
senses.example: The textbook gives a perspicuous account of the theory.

words.note: Perspicuous means clearly expressed; perspicacious means perceptive.

senses.definition: an abundance
senses.example: The market had a plenitude of fresh fruit.

senses.definition: (of speech or writing) using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy
senses.example: The prolix report ran to nine hundred pages.

senses.definition: to reject someone or something in an abrupt or ungracious manner
senses.example: She rebuffed all his attempts at conversation.

senses.definition: an abrupt or ungracious refusal or rejection of an offer or request
senses.example: His proposal met with a sharp rebuff.

senses.definition: (especially of a principle, place or routine) regarded as too important or valuable to be interfered with
senses.example: His Sunday morning walk was sacrosanct.

senses.definition: having or conveying undue or inappropriate interest in sexual matters
senses.example: The tabloid printed salacious gossip about the actor.

senses.definition: making a show of being morally superior to other people
senses.example: His sanctimonious lectures about saving money annoyed his friends.

senses.definition: making or spreading scandalous claims about someone with the intention of damaging their reputation
senses.example: The pamphlet made scurrilous attacks on the mayor.

senses.definition: (of a person or action) showing dedication and diligence
senses.example: The sedulous apprentice practiced every evening.

senses.definition: showy but cheap and of poor quality
senses.example: The shop sold tawdry souvenirs.

senses.definition: sordid or unpleasant
senses.example: The tabloids loved the tawdry details of the affair.

senses.definition: to boast about or praise something, especially excessively
senses.example: The much-vaunted new system crashed on its first day.

senses.definition: lacking in a certain required or necessary quality
senses.example: His plan was found wanting.

words.note: As an adjective, wanting means lacking or not good enough.

senses.definition: shriveled or wrinkled with age
senses.example: A wizened old man sat on the porch.
